fine_lines.title: present perfect vs past perfect
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المضارع التام (have/has + التصريف الثالث) يربط الماضي بالحاضر: Have you ever reported on a storm? الماضي التام (had + التصريف الثالث) لحدث وقع قبل وقت آخر في الماضي: By Saturday night, stores had closed.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Present perfect (have/has + past participle) connects the past to now: Have you ever reported on a storm? Past perfect (had + past participle) is for an action before another past time: By Saturday night, stores had closed.

examples.sentence: I have reported on a blizzard.
We had reported for 48 hours straight.

fine_lines.title: weather vs whether
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الكلمتان تُنطقان تقريبًا بنفس الطريقة. weather = الطقس. whether = ما إذا / هل.
fine_lines.explanation_en: They sound almost the same. Weather = rain, sun, snow. Whether = if.

examples.sentence: I don't know whether it will snow.

grammar.title: Present perfect and past perfect (review)
grammar.explanation_ar: المضارع التام: have/has + التصريف الثالث. نستخدمه لتجربة في أي وقت من الحياة (Have you ever...?) أو لشيء بدأ في الماضي ومستمر (I have wanted this my whole life). الماضي التام: had + التصريف الثالث. نستخدمه لحدث وقع قبل حدث أو وقت آخر في الماضي. ومنه الماضي التام المستمر: had been + فعل ing لفعل استمر مدة قبل وقت في الماضي (I had been waiting for years).
grammar.explanation_en: Present perfect: have/has + past participle, for life experience (Have you ever...?) or something from the past until now. Past perfect: had + past participle, for an action before another past time. Past perfect continuous: had been + -ing for an action that continued before a past time.
examples: Have you ever reported on a big weather event?
I have wanted to report on a big weather event my whole life.
By Saturday night, stores and restaurants had closed.
I had been waiting for that blizzard for years.
